title: Peppermint Candy
events_chronological: At a factory workers' picnic beside a stream, Yong-ho sits apart with Sun-im and tells her he means to be a photographer.
Sun-im gives Yong-ho a tin of peppermint candy, and he watches a train go by feeling that his life is about to start.
Conscripted, Yong-ho is sent with his unit to put down an uprising in a southern city and is shot through the leg.
Frightened and bleeding in the dark, Yong-ho fires at a moving figure and kills a schoolgirl who was only trying to get home.
Now a police detective, Yong-ho beats a student suspect in an interrogation room and discovers he is good at it.
Sun-im comes to the station with a camera she has saved for, and Yong-ho refuses it and sleeps with a waitress the same night.
Yong-ho tortures an activist in a provincial town, then washes his hands and eats a bowl of rice.
Yong-ho marries Hong-ja, a cheerful woman he does not love, and lets his colleagues arrange the wedding.
Yong-ho runs a small furniture business, hits his wife, and finds out she is sleeping with her driving instructor.
Yong-ho follows Hong-ja, catches the pair and beats the man, then goes back to a mistress of his own.
Yong-ho's business collapses, his partner takes what is left of the money, and Hong-ja leaves him.
Yong-ho buys a handgun and drives around the city unable to decide who deserves it.
Sun-im's husband takes Yong-ho to her hospital bed, where she is dying and cannot speak, and hands him back the camera she bought.
Yong-ho gatecrashes a reunion picnic beside the same stream, climbs onto a railway bridge, and stands in front of an oncoming train shouting that he wants to go back.
syuzhet_notes: Seven dated episodes run in reverse: 1999, three days earlier, 1994, 1987, 1984, 1980, 1979. Between them the film holds on a railway line filmed from a moving train and played backwards, so the landscape itself runs the wrong way.
fabula_notes: Chronology is fixed by the captions that open each episode. The suicide told first is the latest event in the story and the picnic told last is the earliest.
